title: Wusun
capsule: The Wusun were a semi-nomadic pastoral people who inhabited the Ili River valley and the Tian Shan region of what is now eastern Kazakhstan and Xinjiang, first attested in Han Chinese sources around 160 BC when they were expelled from the Gansu corridor by the Xiongnu. At their apex in the second and first centuries BC the Wusun controlled a confederacy of some 630,000 people and maintained diplomatic and marriage alliances with the Han dynasty — the 'heavenly horses' tribute and the dispatch of Chinese princesses as royal brides to Wusun kunmo (kings) are recorded in the Han shu. The confederacy weakened under internal succession disputes and Xiongnu pressure in the first century AD, and Wusun references in Chinese records fade after the fourth century AD, with the group likely absorbed into the Rouran or Hephthalite sphere.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is conjectural, reconstructed from Han annals describing grazing ranges and diplomatic correspondence; no administrative boundaries or inscriptions demarcate Wusun territory, and the polygon represents scholarly consensus on their Ili valley heartland.
